key_insight: Y6 excitons are hybrid Frenkel–charge-transfer states with 20–40% charge-transfer character, enabling delocalization-assisted transport and rapid quenching near interfaces.
engineering_relevance: The work provides a quantitative, spectroscopy-driven framework for tuning single-component solar-cell materials and interfaces to improve charge separation and exciton management.
method: Ultrafast transient absorption spectroscopy on Y6 films interfaced with hole-transport layers.
Analytical hybrid Frenkel–charge-transfer model to extract coupling, charge-transfer admixture, and system-bath interaction strengths.
Link experimental quenching dynamics to microscopic transport mechanisms and spatial injection length scales.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~1 ps quenching within ~4 nm of the interface, consistent with a short-range injection mechanism and delocalization-mediated motion.
watch_item: The extracted parameters come from a model-based interpretation, so applicability may depend on how well the hybrid-state assumptions capture morphology and disorder in other materials.
paper_title: Quantitative Analysis of Exciton Composition and Dynamics in Y6 Films for Single-Component Solar Cells
